items.text: Morgan Stanley grants employee loans under a program established primarily to recruit certain Wealth Management financial advisors; the loans are full recourse, generally require periodic repayments, and are due in full upon termination of employment.
items.quote: Employee loans are granted in conjunction with a program established primarily to recruit certain Wealth Management financial advisors, are full recourse and generally require periodic repayments, and are due in full upon termination of employment with the Firm.

items.text: Morgan Stanley sought to claw back recruiting bonus money from a former advisor through promissory notes, loans that brokers pay back to firms over time.
items.quote: Morgan Stanley sued Cohen in 2021 in a dispute over promissory notes, loans that brokers pay back to firms over time. Morgan Stanley sought to claw back recruiting bonus money from Cohen.

items.text: Morgan Stanley sought to claw back $2.46 million in recruiting bonus loans, plus attorney's fees and interest, from a financial advisor.
items.quote: a sole FINRA arbitrator turned aside Morgan Stanley's attempt to claw back $2.46 million in recruiting bonus loans, along with attorney's fees and interest.

items.text: Morgan Stanley is not introducing retention bonuses as part of its 2027 pay plan for advisors; instead it is increasing a pay threshold for advisors by 10% in 2027.
items.quote: Morgan Stanley and Merrill Lynch are not introducing retention bonuses as part of their 2027 pay plans for advisors, adhering to a more traditional approach. As it has in the past, Morgan Stanley is increasing a pay threshold for advisors by 10% in 2027, meaning advisors have to generate that much more revenue to see the same pay next year.

items.text: Morgan Stanley has taken a small amount of an advisor's gross revenue as deferred compensation, requiring advisors to stay for years in order to vest (referred to as golden handcuffs).
items.quote: Giants like Morgan Stanley for years have taken a small amount of an advisor's gross revenue, called it deferred compensation, and required advisors to stay for years in order to vest. If a financial advisor leaves a firm with a deferred compensation plan, he or she forfeits that compensation, which is also known on Wall Street as golden handcuffs.

cells.reason: The passages describe the firm's recruiting/transition compensation, namely employee (recruiting) loans and promissory notes with clawback provisions, plus its 2027 pay-plan approach of increasing the pay threshold rather than adding retention bonuses, and deferred compensation tied to tenure.
